Home.title: SemtSkoru — Istanbul District Livability Score
Home.description: An open-source tool that turns air quality, green space, transportation, parking, healthcare, and public transit access into 0-100 scores for Istanbul's 39 districts, using real İBB open data.
Home.heading: Explore Istanbul Through Data
Home.intro: We turn Istanbul's 39 districts into 0-100 scores across air quality, green space, transportation, parking, healthcare, and public transit access — all backed by real İBB Open Data Portal data, with each score's source and freshness date shown alongside it. Pick a district to see its dimension-by-dimension scores and how they're calculated, or compare two districts side by side and on the map.

Assistant.title: AI District Assistant
Assistant.description: Describe your preferences in a few sentences and see AI-powered district recommendations grounded in the real İBB open-data scores SemtSkoru calculates for all 39 districts.
Assistant.heading: AI District Assistant
Assistant.intro: Describe what you're looking for in a few sentences, and SemtSkoru will recommend 2-3 districts based on the real scores it calculates for all 39. Recommendations are always grounded in real İBB open data — the model never invents anything about Istanbul beyond the numbers it's given.
examples: We're a family with kids — green space and healthcare access matter most, and our budget is tight.
I work remotely — air quality and easy access to public transit matter most to me.

About.title: About
About.description: Why SemtSkoru exists, how we calculate our scores, and what data we rely on - with source, license, and freshness details.
About.heading: About
About.whyBody: Plenty of open-data projects for Istanbul plot data on a map, but don't make it comparable. SemtSkoru distills air quality, green space access, traffic congestion, parking access, healthcare access, and public transit access into a single 0-100 score, so you can explore Istanbul's 39 districts with real data and compare two districts directly. It doesn't offer a preference-weighted "best district for you" recommendation — that's a deliberate scope decision; it shows each dimension on its own and leaves the interpretation to you.
About.howIntro: Every dimension is a real measurement, mapped from raw data to 0-100 with a linear formula — never a guess or a subjective judgment:
About.howFooter: The overall score is a simple average of the dimensions that have data. If a district is missing data for a dimension (for example, districts without an air-quality monitoring station), that dimension is excluded from the average and the interface clearly shows "No data" — it is never filled in by guessing or interpolation.

transportation.freshness: Historical — not live, clearly labeled in the UI

parking.source: İBB İSPARK Open Data Portal (live API)

healthAccess.freshness: Static — the source hasn't been updated since 2024, re-fetched weekly

transitAccess.freshness: Static — infrastructure changes slowly, re-fetched weekly

About.openSourceBody: SemtSkoru is fully open source under the MIT license — all of the code, including the scoring formulas, is public on <github>GitHub</github>. If you find a bug or a data source changes, you're welcome to contribute.

SiteFooter.description: An open-source tool that turns Istanbul districts' air quality, green space, transportation, parking, healthcare, and public transit access into 0-100 scores using real İBB open data.

methodology.airQuality: The AQI (0-500, EPA standard) from İBB's live air-quality monitoring station is mapped to 0-100 by splitting the EPA's 6 categories (Good → Hazardous) into equal bands and inverting them. Lower AQI = higher score.
methodology.greenSpace: A linearly decreasing score based on distance to the nearest park: 0 meters scores 100, 2,000 meters (about a 25-minute walk) or more scores 0.
methodology.transportation: A linear score based on the district's average traffic speed: Istanbul's urban speed limit of 50 km/h or higher scores 100, a full stop (0 km/h) scores 0.
methodology.parking: The average share of open capacity across the district's İBB İSPARK parking facilities (open capacity / total capacity, unweighted average per facility): completely empty (100% open) scores 100, completely full scores 0. This only covers facilities operated by İSPARK, is a small sample, and doesn't reflect on-street parking.
methodology.healthAccess: İBB publishes its "34-Minute Istanbul" Health Index at the neighborhood level; a district's average is the population-weighted average of its neighborhoods' health-access index values (neighborhoods with zero population are excluded from the average). İBB doesn't state that this index itself is on a 0-100 scale, so the MVP linearly scales the lowest and highest district averages actually observed across the real 39 districts to 0-100 (the lowest-scoring district gets 0, the highest gets 100).
methodology.transitAccess: İETT's citywide bus-stop dataset (15,486 stops) is matched to each district's boundary with a point-in-polygon test (since stops' district-code field doesn't offer a reliable name match). Rather than the raw stop count, we use density (stops per km²) — the stop count divided by the district's actual land area (in km², computed with a simple planar approximation scaled to the district's average latitude) — so a district doesn't get an unfair advantage just for being large. This density is then linearly scaled to 0-100 using the lowest and highest values actually observed across the real 39 districts (the lowest-scoring district gets 0, the highest gets 100) — not an official standard, but an honestly documented MVP assumption.
